# Results — Study 1021 (Stability Breeds Instability) on the real tapes

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py) in 31 s. Primary
tape as-of **2018-11-30** (Fama-French monthly, last full month); S&P 500 daily as-of
**2022-11-30**; VIX as-of **2018-12-31** (partial final months dropped). Headline
fingerprint `394be76d78ac`. Null simulations: 400 paths per model, seed 1021.*

## 0. Data provenance

All tapes are read offline through [`quantlab/bundled.py`](../../../quantlab/bundled.py), which
refuses any file whose SHA-256 differs from the pin.

| Tape | Package · file | SHA-256 pin | Label | Span | Rows | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|---|--:|---|
| Fama-French monthly (mkt = Mkt-RF + RF, rf) | `arch` · `frenchdata.csv.gz` | `f23436727b01d879…` | monthly, nominal, **total return** | 1926-07-31 → 2018-11-30 | 1,109 | `394be76d78ac` |
| S&P 500 index (SP500) | `skfolio 1.8.1` · `sp500_index.csv.gz` | `894c34431c284f86…` | daily, nominal, **price only** | 1990-01-02 → 2022-11-30 | 8,294 | `e223c581ae22` |
| CBOE VIX close | `arch` · `vix.csv.gz` | `410bd07360dc798f…` | daily, index level (illustration only) | 2014-01-03 → 2018-12-31 | 1,257 | `377a01738af1` |

The **total-return** Fama-French market (`mkt = Mkt-RF + RF`) carries every return-level
number: drawdowns, terminal wealth, Sharpe. The S&P 500 tape is a **price index** and is used
only for realised volatility from daily returns and a labelled illustration. Everything is
nominal.

## 1. The prolonged-calm score

`rv` = 12-month realised vol; `trend` = its trailing 10-year mean; `low = max(−log(rv/trend), 0)`;
**`calm` = the trailing 5-year mean of `low`** — all past-only, known at the month's close. The
first usable reading is **1942-04-30** (920 months).

| Decade | Calmest month | Peak calm | Mean calm |
|---|---|--:|--:|
| 1940s | 1946-04-30 | 0.641 | 0.469 |
| 1950s | 1950-05-31 | 0.280 | 0.187 |
| 1960s | 1966-07-31 | 0.287 | 0.193 |
| 1970s | 1979-12-31 | 0.138 | 0.064 |
| 1980s | 1986-06-30 | 0.173 | 0.131 |
| 1990s | 1997-02-28 | 0.527 | 0.302 |
| 2000s | 2008-08-31 | 0.511 | 0.214 |
| 2010s | 2018-04-30 | 0.409 | 0.219 |

The primary slope is **+0.0141** — a 1.4%-point
deeper 24-month drawdown per SD of calm, against an

Every long-horizon (H ≥ 12) drawdown, crash and volatility slope points the Minsky way;
the largest HAC t among them is 1.50 — none clears 2.

## 4. The confound — is it more than mean reversion?

Each model is fitted to the real monthly excess returns and simulated 400 times at the
real length, with the real bill path added back; the identical regression (24-month horizon)
runs on every simulated tape. p = share of no-feedback tapes with a slope at least as large
as the real one (one-sided, in Minsky's direction).

| Null | Outcome | Real slope | Null mean | Null 90% band | p |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| GARCH-t | max drawdown | **+0.0141** | -0.0135 | [-0.0437, +0.0169] | **0.077** |
| GARCH-t | P(DD ≥ 20%) | +0.0278 | -0.0398 | [-0.1415, +0.0724] | 0.157 |
| GARCH-t | realised vol | +0.0084 | -0.0115 | [-0.0377, +0.0103] | 0.067 |
| GARCH-t | excess log return | +0.0321 | +0.0081 | [-0.0548, +0.0726] | 0.267 |
| FIGARCH-t | max drawdown | **+0.0141** | -0.0325 | [-0.0928, +0.0149] | **0.057** |
| FIGARCH-t | P(DD ≥ 20%) | +0.0278 | -0.0605 | [-0.1937, +0.0513] | 0.100 |
| FIGARCH-t | realised vol | +0.0084 | -0.0479 | [-0.1459, +0.0073] | 0.045 |
| FIGARCH-t | excess log return | +0.0321 | +0.0724 | [-0.0721, +0.3607] | 0.441 |

GARCH(1,1)-t: ω = 0.956, α = 0.136, β = 0.830,
ν = 7.9 (persistence half-life 20 months). FIGARCH-t:
d = 0.765, φ = 0.043, β = 0.693, ν = 7.4.

This is the table the study exists for. **In a world with no risk-taking feedback, calm is
followed by *smaller* drawdowns** (null mean -0.0135): vol is persistent,
and a quiet market stays quiet for a while. The real slope is positive, so it is
+0.0276 above what mean reversion predicts — that gap
is the Minsky channel's best case, and it lands at **p = 0.077** (GARCH) and
**p = 0.057** (FIGARCH).

| 1942-04-30 → 1979-07-31 | -0.0088 | -0.49 |

The two halves disagree in sign: the second half carries the whole effect (1987, 2000-02 and 2008 all sit in it), the first half points the other way.

## 6. The two horizons — clustering vs the Minsky claim

**Short horizon (daily S&P 500, 1990-2022).** Log monthly realised vol from daily returns has
AR(1) **φ = 0.688** (HAC t = 14.6, half-life
1.9 months, n = 394). Calm this month predicts calm next
month — overwhelmingly.

**Every horizon (Fama-French).** Correlation of today's state with log realised vol over the
6 months starting h months ahead. `low_now` is how far vol sits below trend *today*; `calm` is
the 5-year score; the null columns are the calm correlation on 60 GARCH tapes.

| h (months ahead) | low_now | calm | GARCH null mean | GARCH null 90% |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0 | -0.291 | +0.105 | -0.122 | [-0.355, +0.104] |
| 3 | -0.221 | +0.146 | -0.103 | [-0.335, +0.105] |
| 6 | -0.150 | +0.175 | -0.087 | [-0.314, +0.140] |
| 12 | -0.049 | +0.210 | -0.063 | [-0.299, +0.171] |
| 18 | +0.066 | +0.223 | -0.050 | [-0.300, +0.202] |
| 24 | +0.098 | +0.214 | -0.045 | [-0.275, +0.195] |
| 30 | +0.125 | +0.193 | -0.046 | [-0.254, +0.162] |
| 36 | +0.129 | +0.148 | -0.049 | [-0.275, +0.179] |
| 48 | +0.116 | +0.068 | -0.052 | [-0.279, +0.197] |
| 60 | +0.178 | -0.030 | -0.051 | [-0.307, +0.201] |

`low_now` is the clustering signature: low vol today goes with low vol over the next months
(negative correlation), and the sign only turns positive from about h = 15
months out. The 5-year `calm` score correlates *positively* with future vol at every horizon
up to about four years, while the no-feedback GARCH tapes centre slightly below zero. The real
curve pokes above the null's pointwise 95th percentile at h = 0, 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18, 21, 24, 27, 30, 33
(60 null tapes). Taken at face value this is the strongest-looking evidence in the study, and
it points Minsky's way: prolonged calm goes with *more* volatility one to three years later
than mean reversion allows. But it was not the pre-registered test — these are overlapping,
highly correlated horizons scanned after the fact, the band is pointwise and built on 60 paths
— so it moves the stamp nowhere. It is the first thing a fork should pre-register: calm →
forward 24-month volatility, scored by correlation against a no-feedback null.

## 7. Illustrations — not inference

**Post-1990 S&P 500 (price index, monthly).** The calm score needs 191 months of history, so
on this tape it starts in late 2005 — about one and a half crash cycles.

| Date | Calm | Percentile of its own past | Next-24-month max DD (price) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2006-12-31 | 0.388 | 100% | 42.2% |
| 2007-06-30 | 0.469 | 100% | 52.6% |
| 2014-06-30 | 0.130 | 28% | 8.9% |
| 2017-12-31 | 0.403 | 75% | 14.0% |
| 2019-12-31 | 0.327 | 54% | 20.0% |

**The VIX tape (2014-01 → 2018-12), one episode.** In 2017 the VIX averaged
**11.1**, closed below 11 on 54% of days and
touched 9.14 — the calmest year in the index's history to that point. In 2018 it
spiked to **37.3** (2018-02-05, "Volmageddon") and the S&P 500
price index fell **-19.8%** peak to trough within the year. That is exactly
the story the believers tell — and it is **one** observation on a five-year tape. It cannot
support or refute anything; it is here because it is the picture everyone has in mind.

## 8. Could you trade it?

All legs on the total-return tape from **1952-04-30** (67 years): weight
decided at the close of month t, held through t+1; turnover = one-way × NAV from the drifted
weight; **10 bp** one-way; the cash sleeve earns T-bills. Sharpe is on **excess-of-bills**
returns for every leg.

| Rule | Sharpe gross | Sharpe net | CAGR net | Vol | Max DD | Terminal wealth | Turnover/yr | Avg equity weight |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Buy & hold | 0.496 | 0.496 | 10.91% | 14.7% | -50.4% | 986× | 0.00 | 1.00 |
| Calm de-risk (½ in bills) | 0.488 | 0.487 | 10.38% | 13.6% | -46.4% | 717× | 0.05 | 0.92 |
| Vol-target (unlevered) | 0.457 | 0.455 | 9.69% | 13.0% | -44.4% | 474× | 0.26 | 0.91 |

Block bootstrap (24-month circular blocks, 2,000 draws) of the net excess Sharpe difference:

| Comparison | Δ Sharpe | 95% CI | p(Δ ≤ 0) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Calm de-risk − buy & hold | -0.008 | [-0.067, +0.063] | 0.60 |
| Vol-target − buy & hold | -0.041 | [-0.091, +0.005] | 0.96 |

Cost sweep (net excess Sharpe):

| One-way cost (bp) | Calm de-risk | Buy & hold | Δ |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0 | 0.488 | 0.496 | -0.008 |
| 10 | 0.487 | 0.496 | -0.008 |
| 25 | 0.487 | 0.496 | -0.009 |
| 50 | 0.486 | 0.496 | -0.010 |

The rule was de-risked in **16%** of months. The market's excess return
in those months was **7.9% a year**, against
7.2% in the rest — calm months are not bad months, so stepping out of them gives up premium. At 0.05× NAV a year costs are irrelevant; whatever the rule earns
or loses, it earns or loses on *timing*, not on friction.

## Caveats

- **Few independent crashes.** 92 years of monthly data, but the calm score needs 16 years of
  warm-up and the outcome is a multi-year drawdown: the long-horizon regressions rest on
  ~37 non-overlapping 24-month windows and 7 separate ≥20% drawdowns.
  Any verdict on a crisis predictor at this horizon is low-powered by construction, which is
  why the null comparison (rather than a bare t) carries the inference.
- **US equity drawdowns are not "crises".** Danielsson, Valenzuela & Zer study banking crises
  across 60 countries; this study tests the practitioner's translation — US stock-market
  drawdowns. A null here does not refute their cross-country banking result.
- **The nulls are fitted on the full sample.** They are null-generating processes, not
  forecasters, so no trading rule sees their parameters. GARCH and FIGARCH are two
  mean-reversion shapes; a regime-switching null could be wider still, which would only
  weaken the case.
- **Monthly realised vol from 12 monthly returns is a slow, noisy instrument** on the
  Fama-French tape (no daily data before 1990 here). It is the price of the 92-year window.
- **The robustness grid is shown, not chosen.** The verdict uses only the pre-registered
  definition (10-year trend, 5-year calm, 24-month drawdown).
- **VIX: five years, one episode.** Illustration only.

## Verdict

Produced by `strategy.verdict`, fixed before the run and unit-tested in
[`tests/test_strategy.py`](../tests/test_strategy.py).

**Signal: Weak.** The raw link points the way Minsky said: one standard deviation more prolonged calm goes with a **+1.4%** change in the maximum drawdown over the next 24 months (HAC t = 0.88, which does not clear the bar of 2; non-overlapping t = 0.75 on ~37 independent windows). Because volatility mean-reverts, the real question is whether that beats a world with no risk-taking feedback at all — and there a no-feedback GARCH(1,1)-t fitted to the same tape predicts a slope of **-1.3%**: calm is *supposed* to be followed by calm. Against that null the real slope has one-sided **p = 0.08**, against a long-memory FIGARCH-t **p = 0.06** — it sits in the right tail of both, but short of the 5% line — suggestive, not certified. Forward volatility tells the same story (GARCH p = 0.07). At the one-month horizon the sign is the opposite and certain: log realised vol has AR(1) φ = 0.69 (t = 14.6) on the daily S&P tape. The long-horizon leg rests on only **7 separate ≥20% drawdowns** after the signal starts, and its two halves disagree (-0.9% then +3.9%).

**Tradability: Mirage.** Halving equity when calm is in the top fifth of its own past (decided at the close, held the next month, 10 bp one-way, bills on the cash leg) trailed buy-and-hold: net excess Sharpe 0.49 vs 0.50 (difference -0.008, block-bootstrap p(≤0) = 0.60), with a plain unlevered vol-target at 0.45. Max drawdown -46% vs -50%; terminal wealth 717× vs 986× over 67 years. The rule is cheap to run (turnover 0.05× NAV a year, so costs are not the problem) — the problem is that it sits half out of the market through long calm *bull* runs, and the crashes it partly dodges do not repay the rallies it misses.

> **In one sentence:** Long calm is followed by somewhat bigger drawdowns than a no-feedback volatility model predicts, but not significantly so (raw t = 0.88; GARCH p = 0.08, FIGARCH p = 0.06), and selling the calm moved net Sharpe by -0.01 — "low vol = sell" is a story the tape hints at and cannot cash.
